newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK utilities seek growth through powerful partners.
newsitem.headline: HK utilities seek growth through powerful partners.

text.p: The New Year has just begun but Hong Kong utilities already are shaking off the languor that plagued them in 1996, linking up with powerful partners to ride their coattails into other markets, analysts said on Wednesday.
China Light & Power Co Ltd announced on Tuesday that conglomerate CITIC Pacific Ltd would take a 20 percent stake in the utility.

The news, which gave China Light shares an immediate boost, followed a deal earlier this month in which another Hong Kong conglomerate, Hutchison Whampoa Ltd, raised its stake in Hongkong Electric Holdings Ltd.
"The participation of new parties will bring new horizons. Hong Kong is not exciting -- it is a mature market," said Ben Kwong, director of research at Dharmala Securities.

"Electricity demand just grows very steadily and with six million people (in Hong Kong) there is very limited scope for expansion. But if you can find a partner that can help you expand in China then it is an entirely different story."
Shares in Hong Kong utility companies languished in 1996, providing an opportunity for more dynamic firms to pick them up cheaply and turn them into growth businesses, analysts said.

"In the case of China Light and Hongkong Electric, they have realised that their future is in the PRC (People's Republic of China) and their future is around the region," said one analyst at a regional brokerage.

"They have to evolve from simple Hong Kong utilities to regional power producers and on their own they probably have not got the connections to forge their way into some of these other markets," he said.
Analysts expected increasing Chinese interest in Hong Kong utility companies with the territory reverting to Chinese rule at midnight on June 30.
"In the run-up to 1997 and maybe after 1997, we will see increasing Chinese interest in the utilities sector because it is strategically important," said Kwong.

CITIC Pacific is the Hong Kong-listed arm of China's state trading giant China International Trust and Investment Corp and is expected to provide some clout to China Light in its dealings on the mainland.
"We all believe that this deal has a political motive just to have China owning an interest in a major utility company in Hong Kong," said Percy Au-Young, director of research at DBS Securities.
Thomas Chesser, director of regional power research at BZW Asia, said China Light had about 45 percent overcapacity and Hongkong Electric about 35 to 40 percent overcapacity.

"What that overcapacity means is that both of those companies will be growing at a slower rate because they don't have to build new plants. So I think what China wants to avoid is having two major stocks basically just be dogs," he said.

Forging ties with other companies would not only open avenues for future growth for China Light and Hongkong Electric, but also allow CITIC Pacific and Cheung Kong Infrastructure -- which is due to take Hutchison's Hongkong Electric stake -- to hope for favourable treatment from China, one analyst said.

"I do think that there is some collusion going on between Beijing and these companies in the case of Hongkong Electric/Hutchison and in the case of China Light and CITIC Pacific in trying to resolve the overcapacity problem in Hong Kong before the handover," he said.

China Light said on Tuesday that proceeds of the share placement to CITIC Pacific would be used for new investments in China and elsewhere in Asia. Its shares rose HK$1.10 to HK$34.80 on Wednesday while CITIC Pacific fell HK$1.00 to HK$38.50.
